# Part I: Start Here {.unnumbered .part}

Part I has two routes, and you need only one. Both begin with two chapters of reading that
give you the method: @sec-quarto, why one source that rebuilds every output can be trusted,
and @sec-assistant, how to ask an agent for work and check what comes back.

::: cards
A terminal and Git are routine

:   @sec-fast-path adds Quarto to an existing repository and ends with a report in three
    formats reviewed as a pull request; with Quarto, uv, Git and an agent installed and GitHub's
    `gh` signed in, it is meant to take under an hour.

Starting from zero

:   Six steps in @sec-setup, each with a check you can see, end with a web page and a PDF
    that both say 42, the result of a Python cell's `6 * 7`. Then @sec-first-report: a
    one-page report with one wrong number in it. You find it against its data, record the fix
    with Git, undo a change and read three errors made on purpose, all before any agent edits
    it. Allow about an hour for the setup and 45 minutes for the report, at a desk with a good
    connection.

:::
